conviction_note: The quarter is effectively pre-released: Bullish's own monthly metrics give Q3 adjusted transaction revenue of about $27.5M, and the company's H2 phasing puts Q3 SS&O at about $52.9M at the guide midpoint. That makes adjusted revenue about $80.4M against a disputed consensus of $77.8M to $84.8M. So the reaction turns on the FY SS&O guide, which needs a roughly 22% sequential Q4 step-up into a crypto crash, set against a stock down 33% in 20 days and 45% since the Sept 30 close, with peers at their lows bouncing on their prints. Those offset, so p_up is 51 on an 11.5% absolute move; impact_sum (+0.3) and the scaled number (+0.23) agree that this is close to a non-result.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted revenue. Three estimates disagree: $77.8M and EPS $0.06 (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-10, https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/BLSH/23121), $81.0M and EPS $0.08 (therighttrader.com, https://therighttrader.com/earnings-calendar/blsh), $84.8M and EPS $0.10 (Chartmill, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/BLSH/estimates, snippet only, revised down 9.7% in 3 months). The company gives only a FY2026 SS&O guide of $225-245M, adjusted opex of $225-230M and finance expense of $52-60M (https://bullish.com/us/news-insights/bullish-reports-second-quarter-2026-results), plus an H2 SS&O split of about 45% Q3 and 55% Q4 (Q2 call, https://www.webull.com/news/15398475357316096). The bar is disputed, so every finding that depends on it is capped small. My Q3 estimate is about $80.4M ($27.5M transaction plus $52.9M SS&O), +1.5% against the mean of the two most recent sources.

next_guide.basis: Management narrowed the range on 'improved visibility' and cited signed partnerships coming online, which argues for maintain. The 55% Q4 weighting needs about $64.6M of Q4 SS&O at the midpoint, a 22% sequential step from about $52.9M, while BTC is down about 25% since quarter end and index revenue is AUM-linked. That makes a move to the low end, or a cut, the main downside risk; 'maintain' is the modal outcome, not a confident one.

findings.finding: Q3 adjusted transaction revenue is effectively pre-released at about $27.5M (-8% QoQ from $29.9M) by Bullish's own monthly metrics. July $30.7B x 2.62 bps, August $42.5B x 2.13 bps, September $48.6B x 2.14 bps. The same volume-times-spread arithmetic reproduces Q1 ($38.1M against $38.0M reported) and Q2 ($29.5M against $29.9M reported).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell -10.46% on 2026-11-05, the day the October metrics came out, and -16% on 2026-10-30 when the September volume data drove target cuts. The market trades this line on the monthly release, not on the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: the monthly metrics are public and consensus revenue of $77.8-84.8M already sits far below Q2's $92.6M. It is filed because it pins the transaction line and leaves SS&O and the guide as the only unknowns. If it were not priced, consensus would sit near Q2.
findings.independence: Q1 and Q2 reported transaction revenue validate the method (https://www.chartmill.com/news/external/7757/bizwire-2026-5-14-bullish-reports-first-quarter-2026-results, https://bullish.com/us/news-insights/bullish-reports-second-quarter-2026-results).

findings.finding: Delivering SS&O at the guide midpoint implies Q3 adjusted revenue of about $80.4M (range $76-85M across the FY SS&O range). That is +3.3% against Earnings Whispers' $77.8M, -0.7% against therighttrader's $81.0M and -5% against Chartmill's $84.8M. FY SS&O is $225-245M; H1 is $117.5M (Q1 $54.8M derived as $92.8M adjusted revenue minus $38.0M transaction, plus Q2 $62.7M); 45% of the H2 remainder gives Q3 SS&O of $48.4-57.4M, midpoint $52.9M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's 5.3% revenue beat on record SS&O bought +11.6% on day one, given back the next day. Q1's 2% revenue miss cost -8% premarket.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The lowest estimate ($77.8M) implies Q3 SS&O of about $50M, near the bottom of the guide, so a midpoint delivery is a small beat against that source. If the street sat at the midpoint, all three estimates would cluster near $80M. The bar is disputed, so this is capped small, and it lands inside the company's guide.
findings.independence: Shares the guide document with the next_guide finding. Q1 and Q2 totals come from the company releases (https://bullish.com/us/news-insights/bullish-reports-second-quarter-2026-results).

findings.finding: The FY2026 SS&O guide ($225-245M, 55% of H2 in Q4) needs about $64.6M of Q4 SS&O at the midpoint, about +22% on Q3's implied $52.9M. Since the Sept 30 quarter end, BTC has fallen from about $84k to a $62k low (2026-11-15) with $2.35B of spot ETF outflows in two weeks, and CoinDesk index revenue is AUM-linked. That puts the range at risk of moving to the low end or being cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 the guide was narrowed with the midpoint held and the stock rose +11.6% on the day. A cut has no precedent since the IPO.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced through the 45% drawdown since quarter end. But the lowest Q3 consensus already sits at the low end, so a FY cut below $225M would be new information. If it were fully priced, the street would carry an explicit FY SS&O below the range; no such figure was found.
findings.independence: This is macro-to-company transmission. The company has not confirmed it and said signed partnerships are coming online (https://www.webull.com/news/15398475357316096), which cuts against it. The Earnings Whispers preview flags index revenue pressure from lower crypto prices (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/BLSH/23121).

baseline_tension: The evidence agrees with the balanced skew. The Q3 numbers are known and in line, the downside is a FY SS&O guide cut into a crypto crash, and the upside is a 45% post-quarter drawdown with peers bouncing on their prints. Neither side dominates, so p_up sits at 51 against an implied move of 10.5%.
lessons_applied: Rule 6, disputed bar ($77.8M / $81.0M / $84.8M): the revenue-beat finding was capped from +0.8 to +0.5, p_up moved from 52 to 51 and print_vs_bar from +2.0 to +1.5.
Rule 6, inside the guide: the opex finding went from +0.3 to +0.1.
Rule 5, macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by the company: the next-guide cut risk went from -2.0 to -1.5.
Definition and rule 5, a drawdown is not cheapness: the expectations finding went from +1.0 to +0.5, with the peer bounces kept in their own findings and not double counted.
Rule 2, one_off below operating income: the IFRS mark gain went from +0.3 to +0.2.
